title: Brand mark · Accredited Program mark non-roman versions
slide_intent: Teach designers to account for script structure and reading direction when localizing an identifier. Readers need a familiar hierarchy in their own script.
strategic_value: A stable symbol can connect the movement across languages while the script and orientation serve local readers.
demonstration: The page compares Cyrillic, Simplified Chinese and Arabic marks. Each row pairs a horizontal form with a centered form; the Arabic horizontal arrangement puts the symbol at left.
practical_value: Select the supplied script-specific mark and check its reading direction before positioning it on a print item.

content_islands.name: Script guidance
content_islands.spec: Organize the left text by Cyrillic, Simplified Chinese, and Arabic and Hebrew. Separate typography choices from positioning guidance.

content_islands.name: Horizontal specimens
content_islands.spec: Stack one example for each illustrated script. Keep the symbol consistent while the text and side of attachment vary.

content_islands.name: Centered specimens
content_islands.spec: Align the centered versions in a second column to reveal their shared vertical structure.
